# Safe-rule qualification

<!-- Generated by validation/safe-rule-qualification/qualify.py from probes.yaml and
     dispositions.yaml. Do not edit by hand: change the inputs and regenerate. -->

Every rule that could change text automatically in ruleset 2026.7 (`dc4146941049`) — 97 of 220 — was probed and given one disposition. 23 are qualified and stay automatic; 74 are demoted to diagnostics under the same IDs. The result is ruleset 2026.8 (`94ca278080c8`), in which 23 of 220 rules are automatic: exactly the qualified ones.

## Method

Each rule has sentences in four groups (573 in all), run through `present` under the `natural` profile:

- **normal** — the uses the rule was written for;
- **adversarial** — sentence position, part of speech, participles used as adjectives, pronoun objects, phrasal verbs, infinitive complements, fixed expressions, punctuation and capitalisation;
- **specialist** — legal and procedural, finance and accounting, clinical, technical and software, and government language, wherever the word is plausibly a term there;
- **control** — further ordinary uses, which a qualified rule must still apply.

A rule is qualified only if every sentence it fired on stayed grammatical, kept its meaning at full strength, and left any term of art intact. A rule is demoted if one realistic sentence fails; no context guard was added to keep a rule automatic, no new rule was written, and neither Verify nor the integrity firewall was changed.

Most probes were written before anything was run. After the first run, a second pass added sentences for the rules that the first pass had not settled. `qualify.py` re-runs every probe under both the audited ruleset (frozen verbatim in `validation/safe-rule-qualification/ruleset-2026.7/`, hash checked) and the bundled one. It refuses to write the ledger unless the dispositions, the probes and both rulesets agree; the module docstring lists the checks. `tests/test_safe_rule_qualification.py` holds the ledger to the live engine.

Verdicts: **fails** — the sentence that decided a demotion; **correct** — fired and judged correct (qualified rules); **fired** — fired, on a rule already demoted by a failing sentence; **refused** — matched, and the engine refused to apply it; **not reached** — the matcher did not match.

## Retained

### PS.CLARITY.002 — phrase "due to the fact that" → "because"

- **Category:** phrase — subordinating conjunction ("due to the fact that" -> "because")
- **Reachability:** case-insensitive match of the phrase "due to the fact that" at word boundaries. Scope: prose.
- **Family:** wordy-phrases
- **Disposition:** QUALIFIED_SAFE
- **Rationale:** "Because" is an exact equivalent in every position probed, including legal reasoning and after a negation.
- **Residual uncertainty:** After a copula it gives "The delay is because the supplier failed". Some style guides dislike that construction, but it is grammatical and means the same.

| context | verdict | sentence | under 2026.7 |
|---|---|---|---|
| normal | correct | The meeting was cancelled due to the fact that the chair was ill. | → The meeting was cancelled because the chair was ill. |
| normal | correct | Due to the fact that the office is closed, calls are diverted. | → Because the office is closed, calls are diverted. |
| adversarial | correct | The delay is due to the fact that the supplier failed. | → The delay is because the supplier failed. |
| adversarial | correct | It was not due to the fact that we were late. | → It was not because we were late. |
| adversarial | correct | Largely due to the fact that prices rose, sales fell. | → Largely because prices rose, sales fell. |
| specialist | correct | The claim failed due to the fact that the limitation period had expired. | → The claim failed because the limitation period had expired. |
| control | correct | The system crashed due to the fact that the disk was full. | → The system crashed because the disk was full. |

- **Disposition:** QUALIFIED_SAFE

### PS.CLARITY.005 — phrase "for the purpose of" → "for"

- **Category:** phrase — prepositional ("for the purpose of" -> "for")
- **Reachability:** case-insensitive match of the phrase "for the purpose of" at word boundaries. Scope: prose.
- **Family:** wordy-phrases
- **Disposition:** QUALIFIED_SAFE
- **Rationale:** "For" keeps the purpose reading in every probe. The statutory deeming formula is plural ("for the purposes of") and the phrase matcher does not reach it.
- **Residual uncertainty:** "Paid for the purpose of X" becomes "paid for X". That could be read as a purchase, but the object is almost always the thing the money went on.

| context | verdict | sentence | under 2026.7 |
|---|---|---|---|
| normal | correct | The room is used for the purpose of training. | → The room is used for training. |
| normal | correct | Data is collected for the purpose of improving the service. | → Data is collected for improving the service. |
| adversarial | correct | For the purpose of this letter, we means the council. | → For this letter, we means the council. |
| adversarial | correct | The money was taken for the purpose of fraud. | → The money was taken for fraud. |
| adversarial | correct | The sum was paid for the purpose of the repairs. | → The sum was paid for the repairs. |
| adversarial | not reached | For the purposes of this Act, a child is a person under 18. | → not reached |
| specialist | correct | For the purpose of section 5, a dwelling includes a caravan. | → For section 5, a dwelling includes a caravan. |
| specialist | correct | For the purpose of this Agreement, Business Day means a day on which banks are open. | → For this Agreement, Business Day means a day on which banks are open. |
| control | correct | The vehicle may only be used for the purpose of deliveries. | → The vehicle may only be used for deliveries. |

- **Reachability:** case-insensitive match of the phrase "prior to" at word boundaries. Scope: prose.
- **Family:** wordy-phrases
- **Disposition:** QUALIFIED_SAFE
- **Rationale:** "Before" is an exact equivalent in time and in ranking ("ranks before"). Clinical, conveyancing and gerund complements all read correctly. The adjective "prior" is not matched.

### PS.FRAMING.001 — phrase "it is important to note that" → (deleted)

- **Category:** framing deletion ("it is important to note that " -> nothing)
- **Reachability:** case-insensitive match of the phrase "it is important to note that" at word boundaries. Scope: prose; not in heading.
- **Family:** framing-openers
- **Disposition:** QUALIFIED_SAFE
- **Rationale:** Deletes a frame that asserts nothing, and recapitalises the next word. Mid-sentence and reported-speech matches are refused, not applied.
- **Residual uncertainty:** The frame can carry emphasis in a warning notice. Deleting it keeps the statement but loses the emphasis.

| context | verdict | sentence | under 2026.7 |
|---|---|---|---|
| normal | correct | It is important to note that the deposit is non-refundable. | → The deposit is non-refundable. |
| normal | refused | However, it is important to note that the office is closed. | → refused: deleting this would leave invalid spacing or punctuation |
| adversarial | correct | It is important to note that no refunds are given. | → No refunds are given. |
| adversarial | refused | Staff said it is important to note that the rules changed. | → refused: deleting this would leave invalid spacing or punctuation |
| specialist | correct | It is important to note that this letter does not constitute legal advice. | → This letter does not constitute legal advice. |
| control | correct | It is important to note that prices may change. | → Prices may change. |

### PS.LEXICAL.105 — lemma "alleviate" (verb) → lemma "reduce"

- **Category:** verb ("alleviate" -> "reduce")
- **Reachability:** whole-word, case-insensitive match of the generated forms: alleviate → reduce, alleviates → reduces, alleviated → reduced, alleviating → reducing. Part of speech is used to generate the forms and is not checked when matching. Scope: prose.
- **Disposition:** QUALIFIED_SAFE
- **Rationale:** "Reduce" is correct for pain, symptoms, backlog, congestion and concerns, before a pronoun, and in "alleviates the need for".
- **Residual uncertainty:** "Alleviate" implies relief of suffering and "reduce" does not. In clinical prose the result is plainer, not wrong.

- **Residual uncertainty:** A loader "relocates" an image when it adjusts its addresses. "Moves" is what a non-specialist would understand, but it is not the linker term.

## Demoted

### PS.CLARITY.003 — phrase "at this point in time" → "now"

- **Category:** phrase — adverbial ("at this point in time" -> "now")
- **Reachability:** case-insensitive match of the phrase "at this point in time" at word boundaries. Scope: prose.
- **Family:** wordy-phrases
- **Disposition:** DEMOTED (meaning-shift)
- **Rationale:** In a chronology the phrase refers to a past moment, and "now" moves it to the present. This is the ordinary register of a witness statement.

| context | verdict | sentence | under 2026.7 |
|---|---|---|---|
| normal | fired | At this point in time, we cannot confirm the date. | → Now, we cannot confirm the date. |
| normal | fired | We have no vacancies at this point in time. | → We have no vacancies now. |
| adversarial | fails | The plan was sound at this point in time, but not later. | → The plan was sound now, but not later. |
| adversarial | fired | Is it wise, at this point in time, to proceed? | → Is it wise, now, to proceed? |
| specialist | fired | The court is not persuaded that, at this point in time, an injunction is necessary. | → The court is not persuaded that, now, an injunction is necessary. |
| specialist | fails | At this point in time, the claimant had not been paid. | → Now, the claimant had not been paid. |
| control | fired | No further action is required at this point in time. | → No further action is required now. |

### PS.FRAMING.003 — phrase "it should be noted that" → (deleted)

- **Category:** framing deletion ("it should be noted that " -> nothing)
- **Reachability:** case-insensitive match of the phrase "it should be noted that" at word boundaries. Scope: prose; not in heading.
- **Family:** framing-openers
- **Disposition:** DEMOTED (never-applied)
- **Rationale:** The phrase contains the modal "should". The integrity firewall refuses to delete a modal, so every match is refused and the rule has never changed any text. A rule that can only be refused is not a qualified automatic rule; as a diagnostic it reports the same finding without claiming it was attempted. The firewall is not loosened to let it through.

| context | verdict | sentence | under 2026.7 |
|---|---|---|---|
| normal | refused | It should be noted that the office is closed. | → refused: the change would alter protected information: integrity violation — modal: should -> nothing |
| normal | refused | It should be noted that fees apply. | → refused: the change would alter protected information: integrity violation — modal: should -> nothing |
| adversarial | refused | However, it should be noted that the data is incomplete. | → refused: deleting this would leave invalid spacing or punctuation |
| specialist | refused | It should be noted that the Respondent did not attend. | → refused: the change would alter protected information: integrity violation — modal: should -> nothing |
| control | refused | It should be noted that the figures are estimates. | → refused: the change would alter protected information: integrity violation — modal: should -> nothing |

- **Disposition:** DEMOTED (meaning-shift)
- **Rationale:** "About" is also a preposition meaning "concerning". Before anything but a number it changes or blurs the meaning: "returns about the square root". It is also not idiomatic before an adjective ("about equal").

## Families

Rules that share a word, a spelling or a defect shape, and whether they were judged alike.

- **wordy-phrases** — Multi-word stock phrases replaced by one word. `PS.CLARITY.002` QUALIFIED_SAFE, `PS.CLARITY.003` DEMOTED, `PS.CLARITY.004` QUALIFIED_SAFE, `PS.CLARITY.005` QUALIFIED_SAFE, `PS.CLARITY.006` QUALIFIED_SAFE, `PS.CLARITY.008` QUALIFIED_SAFE, `PS.CLARITY.009` QUALIFIED_SAFE, `PS.CLARITY.010` QUALIFIED_SAFE.
- **framing-openers** — Sentence-initial frames that are deleted. `PS.FRAMING.001` QUALIFIED_SAFE, `PS.FRAMING.002` QUALIFIED_SAFE, `PS.FRAMING.003` DEMOTED.
- **utilise** — Four spellings of one verb, each a separate word rule. `PS.LEXICAL.001` QUALIFIED_SAFE, `PS.LEXICAL.002` QUALIFIED_SAFE, `PS.LEXICAL.003` QUALIFIED_SAFE, `PS.LEXICAL.004` QUALIFIED_SAFE.
- **commence** — Two forms of one verb, each a separate word rule. `PS.LEXICAL.005` QUALIFIED_SAFE, `PS.LEXICAL.006` QUALIFIED_SAFE.
- **synthesise** — British and American spellings of one lemma rule. They stand or fall together. `PS.LEXICAL.227` DEMOTED, `PS.LEXICAL.228` DEMOTED.
- **optimal** — The adjective and the adjective-or-noun. Both fail on the same term of art. `PS.LEXICAL.193` DEMOTED, `PS.LEXICAL.194` DEMOTED.
- **predominant** — The adjective fails when used predicatively. The adverb has no such use. `PS.LEXICAL.201` DEMOTED, `PS.LEXICAL.202` QUALIFIED_SAFE.
- **heterogeneous** — A pair of opposites. Both are terms of art in chemistry and statistics. `PS.LEXICAL.165` DEMOTED, `PS.LEXICAL.166` DEMOTED.
- **clinical-nouns** — Clinical record terms replaced by lay words. `PS.LEXICAL.129` DEMOTED, `PS.LEXICAL.154` DEMOTED, `PS.LEXICAL.175` DEMOTED.
- **multi-word-replacements** — One word replaced by a phrase. It is the shape behind FIELD-001's phrasal-verb failures. `PS.LEXICAL.127` DEMOTED, `PS.LEXICAL.163` DEMOTED, `PS.LEXICAL.174` DEMOTED.

## Residual uncertainty

What remains for the retained rules, as judged:

- `PS.CLARITY.002` — After a copula it gives "The delay is because the supplier failed". Some style guides dislike that construction, but it is grammatical and means the same.
- `PS.CLARITY.005` — "Paid for the purpose of X" becomes "paid for X". That could be read as a purchase, but the object is almost always the thing the money went on.
- `PS.CLARITY.009` — In an intercreditor ranking clause "ranks prior to" is the usual drafting. "Ranks before" says the same thing.
- `PS.FRAMING.001` — The frame can carry emphasis in a warning notice. Deleting it keeps the statement but loses the emphasis.
- `PS.FRAMING.002` — As PS.FRAMING.001.
- `PS.LEXICAL.105` — "Alleviate" implies relief of suffering and "reduce" does not. In clinical prose the result is plainer, not wrong.
- `PS.LEXICAL.213` — A loader "relocates" an image when it adjusts its addresses. "Moves" is what a non-specialist would understand, but it is not the linker term.
- `PS.LEXICAL.223` — Parliamentary "scrutiny" is a named function. The noun is not matched, and "examine" keeps the verb's meaning.

And for the audit itself:

- The probes were written by the same agent that judged them. They cover the dimensions above for every rule, but a probe set is a sample, not a proof. A retained rule could still meet a context nobody thought of. The ledger makes each such context a one-line addition to `probes.yaml`.
- The lemma matcher generates forms by part of speech but does not check part of speech when matching. A retained lemma rule reaches every one of its forms, wherever they occur. The probes for retained rules were written with that in mind.
- A demoted rule is a diagnostic. The engine still matches it and records the match in its plan, but never applies it. `present` and `diagnose` do not list rule diagnostics today, so in practice a demoted rule's matches are not shown to anyone. Like every migrated diagnostic, a demoted migrated rule matches only the base form of its term.
